summary: Intermittent spike of 'door-reader:500' errors in office access logs
description: Starting 2026-03-15 09:12 local time we observed intermittent spikes of 500-level errors originating from the building badge readers. The error signature in the central logging service is 'door-reader:500' and correlates with a surge of failed badge-swipe events across floors 3-5. Impact: employees intermittently unable to enter or exit, occasional tailgating alarms. Initial hypothesis: a recent firmware push to badge readers or a downstream auth service regression. Reproduction steps: 1) Observe logs in central logging (access-logs-prod) around 09:00-09:30 2026-03-15 2) Filter by source:reader-nyc-* and error code 500 3) Note correlation with POST /auth/validate timeouts. Triage done by Facilities and SecOps; paging on-call infra for auth-service. No customer-facing impact. Saved sample log snippets in attachments and linked to Slack thread for cross-team triage.
comments: 2026-03-15 09:25 - Aisha Patel: First noticed during morning rounds, saw dozens of failed swipes. Opening ticket to track and escalate.
2026-03-15 09:40 - Liam Chen: Assigned and investigating. Pulling logs and checking recent firmware pushes and auth-service healthy checks.
2026-03-15 10:05 - Security Bot: PagerDuty alert routed to secops-oncall. Related PD incident PD-7742.
2026-03-15 11:20 - Liam Chen: Found a batch job that refreshed reader credentials at 09:11; auth-service returned 502 for a 2-minute window. Correlating further.
2026-03-16 08:45 - Facilities Ops: Rebooted a subset of badge controllers on floor 4; errors dropped but returned later. Continuing investigation.

2026-03-20 14:02 - Liam Chen: Root cause probable: rotated client cert in auth-service without updating reader controllers. Workaround applied: rolled back rotation for readers. Planning controlled rollout of cert fix with Facilities on 2026-03-22.
2026-03-20 16:30 - Security Lead (Maya Torres): Please add a postmortem and link Confluence runbook for firmware rollbacks after fix is complete.
